exposure: attempted vaginal birth after cesarean delivery (VBAC)
cohort: The study included singleton deliveries to women between 37 and 43 weeks gestation who had a single prior cesarean delivery, drawn from all hospital deliveries in Canada (excluding Quebec) between April 2003 and March 2015.
finding: Attempted vaginal birth after cesarean delivery was associated with significantly higher relative rates of severe maternal and neonatal morbidity and mortality compared to elective repeat cesarean delivery.
mod_finding: Attempted vaginal birth after cesarean delivery was linked to higher relative rates of severe maternal and neonatal morbidity and mortality, with a temporal worsening of infant outcomes associated with VBAC.
